params.body:
In the order modal (bestelbon) the native option lists of **Financiering** and **Taal** both opened at the same spot near the top of the modal, over the **Korting** field, while the fields themselves sit well below. Two fields, one place, is the signature of a box the browser computes somewhere other than where it paints it.

## What it actually was

Not the transform, or not only. Every containing-block-creating property in the ancestor chain of those two selects was measured in a built copy of the modal (the same three stylesheets, the same `.modal / .modal-dialog / .modal-content / .modal-body` shell, Chrome 153). The only transform anywhere in that chain is Bootstrap's own `.modal.fade .modal-dialog { transform: translate(0,-50px) }`, and `.modal.show .modal-dialog { transform: none }` clears it: measured computed value is `none` once the 0.3 s open transition is done. So that one is a 300 ms window, not the standing defect.

What separates the two broken modals from all the others is that **they scroll their own body**:

```css
#createOfferte .modal-content, #createBestelbon .modal-content { max-height: 92vh; }
#createOfferte .modal-body,    #createBestelbon .modal-body    { overflow-y: auto; min-height: 0; }
```

plus `overflow: hidden` on `.modal-content` above it. A field far down that inner, clipped scroller does not get its option list at the field; it gets it at the top of the box — which in this form is exactly where Korting is. Every other modal lets `.modal` itself scroll, which is what Bootstrap does, and none of them shows the defect.

## Scope, checked in the CSS

| Modal | Own scroller before this PR | Affected |
|---|---|---|
| `#createBestelbon` (order) | yes (`.modal-body { overflow-y: auto }`, `.modal-content { max-height: 92vh }`) | yes, reported |
| `#createOfferte` (offer) | yes, the same pair of rules | yes, same construction |
| `#relationModal` (relation picker) | no | no |
| rental modal, `#klantenmodusModal`, `#klantenmodusindexModal`, `#merchant-modal`, XML import | no | no |
| Livewire bid modal (`.ui-modal-wide .ui-modal-body`) | yes, and the `ui-modal-in` keyframe animated a transform | the keyframe is fixed here; its inner scroller is left alone, see below |

So it is not "every select in every modal": it is the two long forms that were given a scroller of their own in September, and they are precisely the two Shane sees it in.

## The fix

- `#createBestelbon` / `#createOfferte`: no box inside a box any more. `.modal-content` loses its `max-height` and its `overflow: hidden`, `.modal-body` loses `overflow-y: auto`, and the modal scrolls itself. The header keeps its place with `position: sticky` (that was the point of the September change: the title must not scroll away), and it carries the top rounding now that the content no longer clips.
- `align-items: safe center` on the dialog: a short form stays vertically centred as today, a form taller than the screen aligns from the top instead of pushing its own top out of the scroll. A browser that does not know `safe` ignores the declaration and behaves as before.
- `.modal.fade .modal-dialog, .modal.show .modal-dialog { transform: none; transition: none }`: while that transform is set the dialog is a containing block and Chrome draws the option list against the untransformed box. The modal already fades through `.fade` on the container; the 50 px slide added nothing. This closes the 300 ms window and any interrupted transition, app-wide.
- `@keyframes ui-modal-in` fades on `opacity` alone, for the same reason.

## Tests

`tests/Feature/ModalDropdownAnchorTest.php`, in the spirit of `StylesheetSyntaxTest`: browser geometry has no harness in this repo and a native option list is a window of the operating system, not DOM, so what is pinned is the cause in the stylesheet — no non-`none` transform/filter/perspective on a modal dialog, content or body; no `overflow: auto|scroll|hidden|clip` on the body or content of these two modals; a header that stays `sticky`. It is tagged `@rule S4-4.14`.

```
php artisan test --filter='StylesheetSyntax|AlpineExpression|BuildContract|Modal|Order|Offer|RulesCoverage'
OK (72 tests, 871 assertions)
```

Docs: finding **X-109** (resolved) and a new screen rule **R S4-4.14** ("a dropdown opens at its own field"; the header stays, the modal scrolls). `docs/bedrijfsregels.html` and the coverage table are generated and stay out of the commit.

## What could not be verified here, and what to check on staging

The native option list is drawn by the operating system, so it is in no page screenshot: headless Chrome does not paint it, and full-screen capture on this machine returns the desktop only (no screen-recording permission for this session). The geometry after the fix was verified field by field in a built copy of the modal — whole-modal scrolling, sticky header, top of a tall form reachable, short form still centred — but the popup itself was not photographed. Worth one look on staging: open the order modal, scroll down, open Financiering and Taal.

## Follow-up, not this PR

- The Livewire bid modal still scrolls its own body (`.ui-modal-wide .ui-modal-body`). Its overlay is a fixed flex box, so giving the scroll back to the overlay is a bigger change than tonight's; the keyframe transform is already gone.
- Shane asked whether these fields should use the project's own `slCombo` instead of the browser's list. My opinion: not worth it for this. A corrected native select is accessible for free — keyboard, type-ahead, the phone's own wheel on mobile, no z-index or clipping to maintain — and `slCombo` would have to be rolled out across many screens to avoid two kinds of dropdown side by side. Worth doing only where a select needs something native cannot give (search over hundreds of options, like the takeover vehicle list), and then as a deliberate pass, not as a fix.
params.title: Select lists in a modal opened in the wrong place
